DIVERSE PATHS X UNIFIED GOALS
Bespoke education for young people aged 12–24 with an EHC plan. Built around relationships, interests and individual learning needs.
Section 41 approved
Our specialist post-16 provisions in Cambridge and Milton Keynes are included on the Department for Education's list of institutions approved under Section 41 of the Children and Families Act 2014.
Relationships first, progress together.
We put relationship building, interest-led learning and social, emotional and academic development at the forefront of what we do.
Our programmes are creative, flexible, holistic and trauma-informed. We match staff to students through their skills, experience and interests.
Understand the learner
Individual attention and care, with support shaped around each young person's learning needs.
Build the relationship
Trusting professional relationships that help young people engage and flourish.
Prepare for what's next
Working with schools, local authorities and other professionals towards education and career pathways.
Two centres, flexible support beyond them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Who we are | Lets Kick It Education
pageCache.text:
Education shaped around the individual
Creative, flexible, holistic and trauma-informed support for young people with a variety of learning needs.
Raising the standard of educational support
At Lets Kick It, we aim to raise the standard of educational support offered to young people in the UK.
We work with local authorities to offer programmes for individuals with a variety of learning needs. Our creative, flexible, holistic and trauma-informed approach helps raise engagement and improve young people's educational and work-based journeys.
An alternative to mainstream schools and college
Our bespoke programmes offer young people aged 12 to 24 with an EHC plan an alternative to mainstream schools and college. Our specialist tutors and coaches provide holistic tuition for young people with additional needs who are out of school or between placements.
Programmes are delivered one-to-one or in small groups. Support can take place in the learner's own home and in the community, as well as through our designated learner centres.
Our team supports learners with SEN, ADHD, ASD, dyslexia, emotional support needs, anxiety, mental health needs and physical disabilities. We aim to create a positive, encouraging and safe environment for learning.
A relationship-led approach
We put relationship building, interest-led learning and social, emotional and academic development at the forefront of our work. We understand the importance of a trusting professional relationship in helping young people flourish and prepare for adulthood.
We match staff to students through skill, experience and interests. Our supportive staff are trained to understand the challenges our students face and give each learner individual attention and care.
Our team liaises with schools, local authorities and other professionals to support re-engagement with a more formal education environment or progression towards a career pathway.
Experienced in alternative provision
Our Course Director, Daniel Smith, has significant experience in the sector and in developing learning programmes, including the foundation and creation of successful alternative provision providers in Cambridge and Milton Keynes.
